message.content: Hey. I just clocked out. My feet are killing me. Can you help me sort out dinner? I’m exhausted and don’t want to overthink it.

content.text: I’m sorry your shift was long, Claire. Let’s keep it simple. Do you want to use the chicken breasts you bought yesterday, or would you prefer a pasta dish? I can pull up a quick recipe for either.

message.content: Chicken. But please, no fancy stuff. Just something that takes less than 30 minutes. I need to get to Hugo’s bedtime story by 7:30.

content.text: Understood. How about a lemon-herb chicken with steamed broccoli and rice? It’s fast, healthy, and Inès usually likes it. I can send you the steps now so you can glance at them while prepping.

message.content: That sounds good. Send it over. Also, can you check if we’re low on any ingredients for tomorrow? I don’t want to go back to the store on a Friday evening.

content.text: I’ve checked your inventory list. You’re out of milk and eggs. I’ve added them to your weekly shopping list. Would you like me to draft a quick message to Julien asking him to pick them up on his way home from work?

message.content: Yes, please. Keep it brief. Just say 'Milk and eggs, please. Thanks.' And set a reminder for me to buy the new running shoes I looked at last week. I need to do it this weekend before I forget.

content.text: Done. Message drafted and scheduled for Julien. Reminder set for Saturday morning. Is there anything else you need before you rest?

message.content: No, that’s it. Thanks. I’m going to put my phone down and just sit for a bit.
